history.title: Act of 4 Dec 2025 package (N01–N03, N09)
history.what: Leave up to 5/4 years, PLN 170,000 severance, paid by the companies themselves, for all staff of support-system companies
history.results: ~1,750 PGG staff on benefits by mid-May 2026; 526 JSW severances by 28 May 2026

history.title: Shield act for power and lignite workers (N11)
history.what: Leave up to 4 years, 12× pay severance

history.title: "Energia" outplacement (R09)
history.what: 310 mining and mining-related workers: action plans, courses, placement, subsidised jobs
history.outcome: Programme period ended; replaced by FST 10.19

history.title: Social Agreement and Aug 2021 amendment
history.what: Closure schedule to 2049; PLN 120,000 severance; SRK transfers allowed until 31 Dec 2023 (Pokój, Jastrzębie III)

history.title: SRK model (after the 2015 Kompania Węglowa recovery plan and Feb 2015 amendment)
history.what: Mines handed to SRK; staff got mining leave or severance
history.results: 9,022 applications and 7,650 benefits by May 2017, incl. 4,962 on leave. NIK (2021): restructuring programmes did not make the sector viable
history.outcome: Replaced by company-run model in 2026. Media report that many who took severance later returned to mining, which led to the 2026 return ban

history.title: RPO WSL outplacement (Measure 7.4.2), e.g. PUP Rybnik (L01)
history.what: Outplacement projects across Silesia

history.title: Act of 28 Nov 2003 on hard-coal restructuring 2003–2006
history.what: "Świadczenie górnicze" for underground staff at most 3 years from pension before 1 Jan 2007; retraining stipends; plan: 12,000 people
history.results: NIK audit (2007) of public funds used

history.title: Regional programmes to soften mining restructuring (Silesia; integrated Małopolska programme for mining, steel and chemicals)
history.what: Regional labour-market and enterprise measures, first outplacement in coal

history.title: PHARE "INICJATYWA"
history.what: Mitigation of social and regional costs of mining and steel restructuring

history.title: Górniczy Pakiet Socjalny (Mining Social Package) under the 1998–2002 reform
history.what: 5-year mining leave, lump-sum severance, social allowances, retraining; voluntary departures
history.funders: State budget plus company funds; PLN 5,383.9m in 1998–2002
history.results: About 67,000 people left mining. Demand exceeded the budget. NIK found the 1999 subsidy was not settled

history.title: Liquidation of the Lower Silesian coal basin (Wałbrzych)
history.what: Severance payments as mines closed from the end of 1990
history.results: Severance money was spent quickly; long-term unemployment and illegal "biedaszyby" pits followed

history.title: ČSM closure: mining ended 31 Jan 2026, preparation plant 28 Feb 2026
history.what: ~400 core staff + 260 contractor staff left in 2025; 750 + 150 left in Jan–Feb 2026; ~670 kept for liquidation
history.funders: OKD (severance CZK 1.3 bn); state (Labour Office, allowance)
history.results: ~1/3 of the 900 had found work by the 2026 report, mostly as drivers, locksmiths or warehouse staff, at lower pay (TN.cz)
history.outcome: Repeats the 2021 toolkit; adds the pension hardship waiver

history.title: Outplacement II
history.what: Nationwide; redundant employees and new employers

history.title: ČSA open-pit mine closure, Most (Severní energetická)
history.what: ~485–500 laid off
history.results: ~1/4 found work at once; 271 of 289 eligible applied for the allowance
history.outcome: Ended; allowance continues for long-duration recipients

history.title: Darkov and ČSA (Karviná) closures; OKD mines transferred to Diamo
history.what: ~2,500 moved to Diamo, ~700 kept; ~1,770 left by end Feb 2021
history.results: Labour Office mobile centres at ČSM, Darkov and ČSA from Nov 2020; Nová šichta with 80+ partner firms; Burza práce app; 1,296 allowance applicants by Jun 2021

history.title: NV 415/2020 reinstates the allowance for OKD leavers
history.what: Surface rate cut from CZK 7,000 to 5,300 for new claims
history.funders: State (MPO); MPO estimated up to CZK 820 m to 2031

history.title: Sokolovská uhelná wind-down (pressure gasification plant Vřesová closed)

history.results: 48 people in Outplacement by Sep 2020 (45 from Sokolovská uhelná)
history.outcome: Firm now SUAS Group; smaller cuts in 2025–26

PL: Working: voluntary departures avoided forced lay-offs on a large scale (1998-2002; 2015-2017).
Not working: cash-only exits in Wałbrzych left long-term poverty; severance without a return ban let workers come back to mines; restructuring did not make the sector viable (NIK 2021).
CZ: Working: help on the mine site (it saves trips to Havířov or Karviná), early retraining for driving licences, and direct contact with employers.
Not working: the 2017 transfer bonus attracted too few people, and new jobs pay well below the ~CZK 50,000 miners earned.
